open_issues: LAL: deadline holder is NOP (unprotected, with a deferral option). NOP elected to defer on 2024-06-01 (HR_defer), after the deadline and lottery, so LAL used #17. This is a post-deadline election, listed in router_2024.POST_DEADLINE_CHANGES, not a data error.

WAS/PHX/MEM swaps can't be written as a rank pool; the JSON rules (WAS protected to NYK, MEM own, PHX own) are exact only when PHX's slot is worse than both MEM's and WAS's. The exact logic is in router_2024.py: if WAS is 1-12, WAS gets min(WAS,PHX) and MEM then swaps for the less favorable of the two if better; if WAS is 13-30, NYK takes it and MEM may swap only against PHX (HR_aug23, explicit).

OKC pool: HR_aug23 gives the general rule (of the picks OKC controls that convey — own, LAC, HOU if 5-30, UTA if 11-30 — UTA gets the least favorable, WAS the second-least, OKC the rest); HR_mar24 states the projected result (WAS the better of LAC/OKC, UTA the worse). The JSON pool follows HR_mar24; router_2024.py encodes the general rule (they differ only if a conveyed HOU/UTA pick lands worse than both the LAC and OKC picks). The 3-pick case is covered by the general sentence but not by an HR worked example (ASSUMPTION in the module).
Draft-night trades (not mismatches; pre-draft holder recorded): #8 SAS->MIN, #14 POR->WAS, #22 PHX<->#28 DEN, #24 NYK->WAS, #26 WAS->NYK->OKC.
Wikipedia's chain annotations for #14/#26 are incomplete (e.g., they omit Portland); holders taken from NBA.com and CBS, which agree.
No 2024 first-round picks were forfeited per the sources checked (league forfeitures in this period were second-rounders).
The executable router router_2024.py is authoritative where the rank grammar can't express the terms; see its ASSUMPTIONS list.
